founder.name: Maria Chen
founder.notes: 10 years multi-unit restaurant operations; most recently Director of Operations for a 42-unit QSR franchise group in the Texas Triangle. Left that role 3 months ago. No stated funding strategy yet.

business_basics.one_liner: Software that lets a multi-location restaurant's shift manager automatically text the right qualified backup workers the moment someone calls out sick, so the shift gets covered in minutes instead of the manager working down a phone list for 45 minutes while the line backs up.
business_basics.business_type_notes: B2B SaaS, hybrid self-serve/sales-led: a single-location GM can self-serve a trial, but real revenue is sales-assisted contracts signed at the multi-unit franchise-group level. Buyer (Director of Operations / Owner-Operator) and day-to-day user (shift manager/GM) are different people. Must integrate with existing scheduling systems (7shifts, HotSchedules named by founder). SMS delivery is a hard requirement, not push notification, because backup workers often don't have the employer's scheduling app installed.

01_market_segmentation.summary: 15 candidate segments identified; shortlisted for Step 2: QSR franchise groups (10-50 units), casual-dining chains, convenience-store retail, home health aide agencies, school districts

02_select_a_beachhead_market.summary: Beachhead selected: QSR franchise groups, 10-50 units, single metro/region — highest score on reach and right-to-win via founder's own network

03_build_an_end_user_profile.summary: End user profile drafted from 3 real conversations: GM/shift manager at one location of a 10-50 unit QSR group, no budget authority, measured on labor cost % and on-time-opening

04_calculate_the_tam_for_the_beachhead_m.summary: Bottom-up beachhead TAM = $118M/year (66,000 locations x $1,788/year); source: founder estimate, unvalidated group count

05_profile_the_persona_for_the_beachhead.summary: Persona: Jordan Vasquez, GM at a 14-unit QSR group — grounded in real interview

06_full_life_cycle_use_case.summary: Full life cycle mapped across 8 stages for Jordan Vasquez; biggest drop-off risk: onboarding/first use

07_high_level_product_specification.summary: 6 Must-have capabilities defined, traced to the FLCUC; core flow: SMS call-out broadcast, first-accept-wins, target 8 min time-to-cover

08_quantify_the_value_proposition.summary: Quantified value = ~$6,000/yr per location vs. status quo call list; gap judged marginal-to-sufficient, resting on an unproven 8-minute target

09_identify_your_next_10_customers.summary: 7 of 10 real prospects identified; beachhead accessibility: partially validated (network depth thinner than Step 2's reach score implied)

10_define_your_core.summary: Core: cross-location reliability-data pool (design bet, not yet earned); resulting advantages: faster time-to-cover, multi-group pool draw; verdict: moat only today, not yet a true core

11_chart_your_competitive_position.summary: Axes: speed of coverage vs cross-location reach; position: fast+cross-location target position currently unoccupied (unverified); defensibility: contestable until Core exists

12_determine_the_dmu.summary: DMU mapped: ~2-3 distinct roles typical; champion = ambiguous, economic buyer = Director of Operations

13_map_the_process_to_acquire_a_paying_c.summary: 6-stage acquisition path mapped; riskiest stage: franchisor IT/brand-standards check (Stage 4), brand-dependent and unresolved

14_calculate_the_tam_for_follow_on_marke.summary: Pin 2 (casual dining) TAM = $70.8M/yr, founder estimate; Pin 3 (convenience retail) not sized — no basis yet

15_design_a_business_model.summary: Selected model: per-location monthly subscription sold at the franchise-group level; freemium/usage-based/take-rate rejected as DMU- or compliance-mismatched

16_set_your_pricing_framework.summary: Pricing: $149/location/month standard, $129/location/month volume tier (11+ locations); untested with real prospects

17_calculate_the_ltv_of_a_customer.summary: Blended LTV = $52,503 per signed group contract (22-location avg, $129/mo volume tier, 74% margin, 25-month lifetime); all inputs low confidence, unmeasured

18_map_the_sales_process_to_acquire_a_cu.summary: Sales cycle ~68 days, 3.6% aware-to-signed conversion, ~37.8 founder-hours per closed customer; entirely warm-network-sourced, no paid channel modeled

19_calculate_the_coca.summary: COCA = $3,213/customer, LTV:COCA ~16.3:1, 1.5-month payback — flagged as misleadingly optimistic since it excludes any paid/scalable channel

20_identify_key_assumptions.summary: 29-item register swept from Steps 1-19; 8 ranked leap-of-faith assumptions identified, top 3: unproven value-prop target, non-scalable warm-network COCA, onboarding adoption risk

21_test_key_assumptions.summary: All 8 leap-of-faith assumptions deferred (idea stage, no MVBP live yet); biggest open risk carried forward: cross-location pool assumption is testable today at zero cost and has not been tested

22_define_the_mvbp.summary: MVBP: SMS broadcast + first-accept-wins for one pilot group at full price ($129-149/location/mo), manual onboarding, success = 3 real call-outs covered in 30 days

23_show_that_dogs_will_eat_the_dog_food.summary: No usage evidence exists yet — no MVBP customer sold. Honest read: not yet measurable.

24_develop_a_product_plan.summary: Roadmap gated on MVBP shipping + cross-location-pool test; flags an unresolved engineering-resourcing gap across the whole plan

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes hourly backup workers are willing to be on a shared on-call list across multiple nearby locations (even different franchise owners) rather than just their home location.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Ask this directly in the next 10 backup-worker conversations (feeds Step 9); if resistance is high, the beachhead may need to narrow to single-owner multi-location groups only, not cross-owner pools.

key_assumptions.statement: Competitive intensity scores for convenience-retail and home-health segments are estimated, not researched.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Direct competitor search before either segment is considered as a follow-on market (feeds Step 14).

key_assumptions.statement: End user profile is based on only 3 real GM conversations (11 of the founder's 14 total conversations were with Directors of Operations, not the end user role this step profiles) — not yet validated by a broader sample.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Conduct at least 10 more interviews specifically with GMs/shift managers (not ops directors) matching this profile before treating it as validated.

key_assumptions.statement: The 3,000-group and 22-locations-per-group figures are founder estimates from personal network familiarity, not a published/independently sourced count.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Cross-check against a published trade-association member count or a paid market report before this figure is used in any external-facing (investor) context.

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes GMs like Jordan will actually adopt the tool during onboarding rather than defaulting back to the paper call list under shift pressure — not yet observed, since no pilot has run.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Track first-30-days actual broadcast usage per GM during the MVBP pilot (Step 22/23), not just contract signature.

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes CSV import (no live API) is an acceptable onboarding friction point for Directors of Operations at this beachhead size — not yet tested with a real buyer.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Test the actual CSV import flow with the Next 10 Customers (Step 9) during early sales conversations; if it's a stated blocker, API integration may need to move up in priority.

key_assumptions.statement: The 8-minute time-to-cover target and the 70% late-opening-reduction estimate that the entire quantified value proposition rests on are founder targets, not measured pilot results.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Measure actual time-to-cover and late-opening incident rate during the Step 22 MVBP pilot before presenting this value figure as validated in any external context.

key_assumptions.statement: Founder has identified only 7 of 10 target next customers with a real access path; the remaining 3 are unfilled rather than padded. Beachhead accessibility beyond the first ~7 organizations is unproven.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Attend the next regional IFA chapter meeting and the independent-QSR-operators group's next event specifically to identify 3+ more named prospects within 60 days.

key_assumptions.statement: The cross-location reliability-data Core is a design bet, not a current asset — no real usage exists yet to generate the data that would make it a true Core.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Revisit this step once the Step 22 MVBP has real broadcast/acceptance data across at least 2 locations in the same metro; until then, treat 'Core' language in any external-facing plan as aspirational, not established.

key_assumptions.statement: Positions for 7shifts/HotSchedules open-shift features, Sling, and Deputy on the competitive chart are estimated from general category familiarity, not verified via direct research (no WebSearch or product trial performed this session).
key_assumptions.test_plan: Run direct product trials or at minimum a WebSearch/documentation review of each named competitor's actual open-shift/broadcast feature and pricing before this chart is shown to a council or investor.

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes franchisor-level IT/brand-standards approval is not required for most Step 9 target groups — not yet confirmed for any specific brand.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Ask directly in the first real sales conversation (prospect #1, Alex Torres) whether their franchise agreement requires franchisor sign-off on third-party ops tools.

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes Directors of Operations will want a paid pilot at a subset of locations before committing the full group, rather than signing a full-group contract outright — not yet tested with a real prospect.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Ask this directly in the first real sales conversation with prospect #1 (Alex Torres, Copperline Burgers).

key_assumptions.statement: The 2,200 casual-dining-group count and 18-locations-per-group figures for Pin 2 are founder estimates extrapolated from the Step 4 QSR method, not independently sourced.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Validate via a trade-association count or market report before this figure is used in any external-facing context.

key_assumptions.statement: Pin 3 (convenience retail) TAM was not calculated — founder has no basis for a group-count estimate in this vertical and no existing network relationship there.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Revisit only once Pin 2 is underway and a real relationship into convenience retail exists.

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes Directors of Operations prefer per-location monthly subscription pricing over a single flat group-wide fee — not yet validated with a real prospect conversation.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Ask directly in the first 5 real sales conversations (starting with Step 9's prospect #1) whether per-location pricing feels fair vs. a flat group fee.

key_assumptions.statement: Proposed price of $149/location/month is untested with prospects; anchored only to Step 8's unproven value estimate and an unverified sense of incumbent (7shifts/HotSchedules) pricing.
key_assumptions.test_plan: State this price in the next 5 real sales conversations (starting with Step 9's prospect #1, Alex Torres) and record reactions before treating it as final.

key_assumptions.statement: No cohort data yet; LTV uses an assumed 4%/mo churn (25-month expected lifetime) based on a general vertical-SaaS category benchmark, not founder data or a cited specific benchmark study.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Recompute from actual cohort retention once 6+ months of paying-customer data exists.

key_assumptions.statement: 74% gross margin is a founder estimate blending typical SaaS costs with an unmodeled per-SMS variable cost; no actual SMS vendor quote or built cost model exists yet.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Get an actual SMS vendor (e.g., Twilio-class provider) volume quote and rebuild the margin estimate before this LTV figure is used in any external-facing context.

key_assumptions.statement: Step 4's beachhead TAM used the standard $149/location/month rate for all locations, but the average 22-location group actually qualifies for Step 16's $129/location/month volume tier — Step 4's TAM is therefore overstated relative to Step 16's own pricing tiers and has not been reconciled.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Recompute Step 4's TAM using the blended/volume-tier price before presenting the TAM figure alongside this LTV figure in the same document.

key_assumptions.statement: No real funnel data yet; all stage conversion rates and time-in-stage figures are founder estimates, not measured from actual prospect conversations — the Step 9 pipeline has not yet advanced anyone past 'in conversation.'
key_assumptions.test_plan: Recompute from actual funnel data once the first 5-10 real prospects have moved through the process.

key_assumptions.statement: The entire funnel is sourced from Maria's existing warm network (Step 9 found only 7 real named prospects total) — this cost/conversion model has no paid-marketing or outbound-cold channel in it, and does not represent what acquisition would cost once the warm-network list is exhausted.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Model a paid/outbound channel's likely cost and conversion once the warm-network pipeline (Step 9) is exhausted, before presenting COCA as representative of the business at scale.

key_assumptions.statement: Founder time in the sales process valued at $85/hr (unvalidated placeholder) for COCA loading, since no market comp has been formally sourced.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Replace with a sourced local market salary comp for an equivalent AE/SDR role.

key_assumptions.statement: The 16.3:1 LTV:COCA ratio and 1.5-month payback are built entirely from a non-scalable warm-network acquisition channel and should not be presented as representative of unit economics once paid/cold channels are required to grow past the initial ~7-28 warm leads.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Recompute COCA and the ratio once a paid or cold-outbound channel has been tested with real spend and real conversion data.

key_assumptions.statement: Step 15 noted, in prose only, that a marketplace/take-rate business model would likely raise wage-and-hour compliance questions given backup workers are existing employees of the franchise group — this was never logged as a structured assumption or risk_log entry until the Step 20 sweep. The chosen model (subscription) avoids this specific issue, but the observation itself was at risk of being lost.
key_assumptions.test_plan: No action needed unless a future pivot reconsiders a take-rate/marketplace model — if so, get real legal review before proceeding, not an AI-generated compliance read.

key_assumptions.statement: Assumes manual onboarding (no self-serve roster import) is acceptable to the pilot buyer at full price for the first customer — not yet tested, since no pilot has run.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Directly observable outcome of the first MVBP sales attempt itself.

key_assumptions.statement: No usage instrumentation or real customer exists yet; adoption/retention signal cannot be measured. This step cannot be meaningfully completed until Step 22's MVBP has at least one real paying customer.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Instrument core workflow completion (broadcast sent to accepted to shift covered) and login/usage frequency from day one of the first MVBP pilot; revisit this step once 30 days of real usage data exists.

key_assumptions.statement: No step in this plan (1-23) established who actually builds the MVBP — Maria's background is operations, not engineering, and no technical co-founder or contractor has been identified.
key_assumptions.test_plan: Founder needs to resolve this before the Step 22 MVBP timeline is credible — either learn to build a minimal version, bring on a technical co-founder, or hire a contractor.

risk_log.description: Structural / automation-bias (failure mode 3): plan/business-plan.md v1 has no 'Confidence & Validation Status' section, required by docs/AI-RISK-FRAMEWORK.md immediately after the executive summary. Neither skills/business-plan/assemble-business-plan/SKILL.md's delegation instructions to business-plan-editor (§7) nor agents/business-plan-editor.md's own 'Section structure' list this section anywhere, so the writing agent has no instruction to produce it. BLOCKING per skills/risk/ai-risk-review's gate logic. Resolution: add the section (Validated claims / Unvalidated assumptions still open / AI-risk findings still open / what-this-plan-is-not) and, separately, patch agents/business-plan-editor.md's Section structure list and skills/business-plan/assemble-business-plan/SKILL.md §7 so future assemblies include it without manual intervention.
risk_log.status: mitigated — note: fix applied by hand to this one plan file for QA purposes; the underlying skill files (agents/business-plan-editor.md, skills/business-plan/assemble-business-plan/SKILL.md) were NOT patched, so this will recur on every other business's first assembly until round 3 fixes the skill, not just this artifact. See docs/QA-FINDINGS-ROUND2.md.

risk_log.description: Unsourced claim (failure mode 1): plan/business-plan.md states the LTV figure '$52,503 per signed group contract' as fact in the Executive Summary, Section 4, and the Step 17 Appendix entry, but no quantitative_claims entry exists for this figure specifically. plan/17-calculate-the-ltv-of-a-customer.md's own 'Quantitative claims logged' section was left with no qc-017-ltv entry (only key_assumptions ka-017-churn/ka-017-margin/ka-017-step4-price-mismatch were logged). qc-019-ltv-coca-ratio's source field cites the LTV value in prose but is not a substitute for the LTV figure having its own sourced entry. BLOCKING per the Data Contract's 'every number in plan/business-plan.md as fact must have a quantitative_claims entry' rule. Resolution: add a qc-017-ltv entry to business-state.json (and re-open plan/17-calculate-the-ltv-of-a-customer.md to add it there too) before this plan can pass the gate.
risk_log.status: mitigated — qc-017-ltv entry added to business-state.json and plan/17-calculate-the-ltv-of-a-customer.md. See docs/QA-FINDINGS-ROUND2.md for why this slip happened in the first place (Step 17's own SKILL.md gives no mechanical check that every 'Quantitative claims logged' heading actually got a JSON block under it).

risk_log.description: False precision (failure mode 2, advisory): plan/business-plan.md states $52,503 (LTV), $118M (beachhead TAM), $70.8M (Pin 2 TAM), and $6,000/year (value proposition) to 3-5 significant figures throughout, despite every input to each calculation being a round founder estimate or category benchmark with confidence: low. None of these figures can honestly be defended to the stated precision. Advisory, not blocking on its own, but compounds the automation-bias concern in ar-shiftcover-001 — recommend rounding (e.g. 'roughly $50K', '~$120M') wherever these figures appear outside the Appendix's full-derivation detail.
